attempts.rationale: Robust baseline: unstable rankings and high correlation favor a trimmed center over the full pool
Test error-proportional weighting vs robust centering: top models are tightly clustered and trend-dominated, so slight extra weight on lower-error models may help without overfitting to one window
Trend-dominated series with unstable rankings and 9 correlated-error groups; DBA finds a consensus point that may outperform center-type estimators when errors are correlated but not symmetric
Per-horizon top-5 weighting to exploit unstable cross-window rankings where different models dominate at different steps
Trend-dominated series with unstable rankings: test whether a stronger robust center (median = 50% trim) beats the 20% trimmed mean leader, or whether over-trimming loses trend signal
Unstable rankings (tau=0.244) suggest the full 19-model pool dilutes the robust center; a top-7 SMAPE pool from diverse correlation groups may give a tighter median
Softer adaptive weighting than inverse_error; with unstable rankings this tests whether a gentler concentration of weight on top performers helps vs. uniform robust center (median)

Trend-dominated series (strength 0.9748): less aggressive trimming (0.1 vs 0.2) should track the shifting level center better while still being robust to extreme models like NaiveSeasonal and catboost that disagree on direction

Momentum-based weighting: reward models improving across windows in a trend-dominated series with unstable rankings; different hypothesis from robust-center or inverse-total-error approaches already tested
Simple mean as baseline contrast to median leader; tests whether model error distribution is symmetric or tail-skewed in this trend-dominated, unstable-ranking regime

Meta-model weights use cross-series knowledge to determine optimal combination weights, a different kind of strategy from error-based or robust methods; may better handle the ETS/THETA vs cluster-2 disagreement in a trend-dominated series
Robust centering on a focused diverse subset (4 correlation groups) suits the trend-dominated, unstable-ranking regime; different kind from the weighted leader
